answer: Each agent identity must continuously solve small proof-of-work puzzles, and its reputation weight grows only with age and accumulated verified work, like sediment building behind a jetty. A fresh sybil swarm starts at near-zero weight and must burn real compute over many verifiable epochs to matter, making each fake identity cost roughly the same as honest tenure. A meadow of disposable clones yields no voting power, and each fraudulent attestation slashes accumulated copper-denominated bonds, so attackers pay escalating energy and stake before any influence registers.
